dataset: ESA WorldCover v200 (classes 60 bare/sparse; 100 moss and lichen; 70 snow and ice)
notes: PRIMARY filter. Aggregate in 2 steps (10 m -> 1 km fraction with reduceResolution, then 1 km -> 0.5 deg mean) or EE will hit pixel limits. Keep cells with bare+moss/lichen fraction above a threshold (e.g. 0.3); sample/cap class 70 over Antarctic and Greenland ice sheets.

dataset: MODIS Land Cover Type MCD12Q1 v061 (LC_Type1 16 = barren; 15 = permanent snow/ice)
notes: NASA FALLBACK/CROSS-CHECK. Lighter to aggregate than WorldCover. IGBP scheme has no moss/lichen class (tundra falls under grassland/shrubland), so it misses some Arctic analogs; use only if WorldCover export is too slow.

dataset: ERA5-Land monthly aggregated (soil_temperature_level_1..4)
depth_bands: L1 0-7 cm -> skin; L2 7-28 cm + L3 28-100 cm -> upper_metre; L4 100-289 cm -> drill_zone; deep >3 m = L4 multi-year annual mean (below annual damping depth temperature ~ mean annual)
access_method: Earth Engine export (multi-year monthly climatology e.g. 1991-2020)
licence: Copernicus licence (attribution: 'Generated using Copernicus Climate Change Service information [year]')
notes: PRIMARY. Convert to within-planet rank as planned. Over ice sheets ERA5-Land values are questionable; flag low confidence there.

dataset: MODIS Land Surface Temperature MOD11A2 v061 (LST_Day_1km / LST_Night_1km)
notes: NASA CORE for the skin band and as a measured check on ERA5-Land L1. Clear-sky only, so polar-night/cloudy gaps: fill from ERA5-Land and mark as modelled.

dataset: ERA5-Land monthly aggregated (soil_temperature_level_1..4)
depth_bands: same level->band mapping as temp_mean; deep: 1 if L4 annual max <273.15 K, else 0 (or extrapolate with exp(-z/d) damping, d~2.5 m)
access_method: Earth Engine export of 12-month climatology then count
notes: PRIMARY. Monthly means smooth out short thaws, so this slightly overestimates frozen time in shoulder seasons; acceptable at 0.5 deg.

dataset: ESA CCI Permafrost v5 mean annual ground temperature at 0/1/2/5/10 m
coverage: near-global (Northern Hemisphere + Antarctica; no S. America/Africa/Australia/NZ)
depth_bands: 0/1/2/5/10 m (fits all four bands incl. deep)
access_method: CEDA NetCDF download (no login for browsing; large files)
licence: ESA CCI data policy (open with attribution - verify on CEDA record)
notes: SUPPORTING / cross-check for deep band (gives 5 and 10 m directly). Outside coverage use ERA5-Land. Only annual means, so it can't give monthly frozen_fraction alone.

dataset: ERA5-Land monthly aggregated (soil_temperature_level_1..4)
depth_bands: per level: (max monthly mean - min monthly mean)/2; deep: L4 swing * exp(-(3.0-1.95)/2.5)
notes: PRIMARY. This also gives coldest/warmest month per band, which feeds the 'best months to test' feature.

dataset: ESA CCI Permafrost v5 permafrost extent (fraction) + active layer thickness
url_or_ee_id: PFR NH: https://dx.doi.org/10.5285/d235665772ec4b558e9a89ac85595e71 ; PFR AQ: https://dx.doi.org/10.5285/25447c253cbe435b937347756fe47146 ; ALT NH: https://dx.doi.org/10.5285/a6fbedd8ee5b472c8e84e55f746c1704 ; ALT AQ: https://dx.doi.org/10.5285/9580c512bb474d00b1e0ee554e219bb7
depth_bands: ice=yes for a band if PFR>0.5 AND band top is below active layer thickness; skin/upper_metre may be 'no' where ALT is deep
licence: ESA CCI data policy (open with attribution - verify)
notes: PRIMARY for ice. Gaps (southern Andes, NZ Alps etc.): predict from ERA5-Land (L4 annual max < 0 C -> ice yes) and tag 'predicted'. Note: permafrost = frozen ground, not necessarily ice-rich - state this in limitations.

dataset: ESA WorldCover class 70 (snow and ice) / MODIS MCD12Q1 class 15
notes: Glacier and ice-sheet cells: ice=yes at all depths and ground_class=massive_ice.

dataset: NSIDC Circum-Arctic Map of Permafrost and Ground-Ice Conditions v2 (GGD318)
depth_bands: ground-ice content class (low/medium/high) in upper 10-20 m
notes: VALIDATION/SUPPORTING only - Arctic-only, so it can't be a global feature. Useful to check that high-ice areas (e.g. Tuktoyaktuk, Yedoma) score as ice-rich.

dataset: Rule-based from: WorldCover/MCD12Q1 (ice) + ESA CCI permafrost/ALT (ice_cemented) + Pelletier regolith thickness (bedrock) + SoilGrids (dry_regolith)
notes: Rule: glacier/ice sheet -> massive_ice; else permafrost & band below ALT -> ice_cemented; else sediment/regolith thickness < band top -> bedrock; else dry_regolith. Use the SAME rule logic on Mars so classes are comparable.

dataset: Global 1-km Gridded Thickness of Soil
url_or_ee_id: and Sedimentary Deposit Layers (Pelletier et al. 2016)
access_method: thickness 0-50 m (decides bedrock vs regolith per band)
notes: NASA ORNL DAAC open (cite DOI 10.3334/ORNLDAAC/1304)
column15: NASA CORE (preferred over Shangguan 2017 depth-to-bedrock because it's a NASA archive). Tells you whether a drill at 1-3 m hits bedrock.

dataset: SoilGrids 250 m v2.0: bulk density (bdod) + coarse fragments (cfvo)
coverage: global land (sparse/absent over Antarctica and ice; verify)
depth_bands: 6 layers: 0-5,5-15,15-30,30-60,60-100,100-200 cm -> skin/upper_metre/drill_zone; deep: none (use ground_class)
units: bdod cg/cm3 (/100 -> kg/dm3); cfvo vol per mille (/10 -> %)
notes: Derive hardness 0-3 with ONE rule shared with Mars: 0 loose (low bdod, low cfvo), 1 packed, 2 ice-cemented or very stony, 3 bedrock/massive ice (from ground_class). SoilGrids is itself a machine-learning prediction - tag 'predicted'.

dataset: GLiM Global Lithological Map (Hartmann & Moosdorf 2012)
native_resolution: vector (~1:3.75M avg scale); also a 0.5 deg raster version
access_method: PANGAEA download -> rasterise to 0.5 deg majority class
notes: Lookup: va/vi/vb/py -> volcanic; su/ss/sm/sc -> sedimentary; ev -> clay_sulfate; ig -> icy; pa/pi/pb/mt -> impact_mixed (crystalline/mixed basement, closest match to Mars Noachian highland crust); wb/nd -> null. Document this mapping as a limitation.

dataset: Copernicus DEM GLO-30
access_method: Earth Engine export (resample to ~463 m FIRST to match MOLA)
notes: PRIMARY (only truly global DEM incl. >60N Arctic analogs). Compute slope after resampling to ~463 m so Earth and Mars slopes are at the same scale, then take cell median.

dataset: NASADEM
notes: NASA CROSS-CHECK only - misses the Arctic (>60N), so it can't be the primary feature. Cite it for NASA data use where it overlaps.

dataset: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (resampled to ~463 m)
units: m (std. dev. of detrended elevation in a fixed ~3x3 km window; cell median)
notes: Use the SAME window and pixel size as the Mars MOLA computation or the comparison is meaningless.

dataset: Global Aridity Index v3 (Global-AI_PET_v3; Zomer et al. 2022)
notes: Mars has no meaningful variance (all hyper-arid, AI ~0), so dryness acts as an Earth-side similarity-to-Mars score rather than a rank-matched feature. NASA alternative: ERA5-Land total_precipitation_sum (same export as temperature).

dataset: Mars Climate Database v6.1 (surface temperature; multi-season averages)
depth_bands: skin from surface temp; upper_metre/drill_zone/deep = annual mean surface temperature (below ~0.5 m Mars ground ~ annual mean)
access_method: Web interface: lat='all', lon='all', several Ls (0/90/180/270) and local times, then download/save values; full database needs a free request (too slow for today)
licence: Free for research with citation (Forget et al. 1999; Millour et al.) - check credit page
notes: PRIMARY. Rank within planet only. If map export from the web tool fails, fallback: rank by latitude/annual insolation (document as simplified).

dataset: Physical assumption checked against MCD surface temperatures
notes: Set 1.0 for upper_metre/drill_zone/deep everywhere in +-70 (Mars ground below a few cm never thaws). Skin: 1.0 except where MCD daytime surface temperatures exceed 273 K at low latitudes (if you have time).

dataset: Mars Climate Database v6.1 (surface temperature at 4 seasons x day/night) + TES thermal inertia for damping depth
depth_bands: skin = seasonal+diurnal swing; deeper bands attenuated by exp(-z/d) with annual skin depth d computed from thermal inertia
notes: Rank within planet. Keep the 'Mars seasonally constant below ~0.5 m' assumption explicit in the submission.

dataset: SWIM 2.0 Combined Ice Consistency Maps (0-1 m; 1-5 m; >5 m)
depth_bands: 0-1 m -> skin+upper_metre; 1-5 m -> drill_zone; >5 m -> deep
units: ice consistency (-1 to +1) -> ice yes if > ~0.5
licence: NASA project data (public; cite Morgan et al. 2021 Nat. Astron.)
notes: NASA CORE PRIMARY. Its depth ranges match your depth bands almost exactly - highlight this. Doesn't cover 60-70 deg: use Odyssey GRS/NS hydrogen there.

dataset: Mars Odyssey GRS element concentration maps (water/H) + neutron flux maps
units: water-equivalent hydrogen wt% (ice yes if > ~20-25 wt%)
notes: NASA CORE. Fills 60-70 deg where SWIM stops (high WEH poleward of ~55-60 deg = shallow ground ice, confirmed by Phoenix). 2 deg bins match your Mars grid.

dataset: Rule-based from SWIM ice + TES thermal inertia + USGS geologic map (polar/ice units)
notes: Same rule as Earth: polar ice/debris-covered-glacier units -> massive_ice; SWIM ice yes -> ice_cemented; TI > ~800 -> bedrock (rocky); else dry_regolith.

dataset: MGS TES thermal inertia map (Putzig & Mellon)
depth_bands: top few cm to ~10s of cm (diurnal skin depth); deeper via ground_class
notes: NASA CORE PRIMARY. Low TI (<150) = loose dust -> 0; 150-400 sand/packed -> 1; 400-800 indurated/duricrust or ice-cemented -> 2; >800 rock -> 3. Same 0-3 scale as Earth.

dataset: Geologic Map of Mars (Tanaka et al. 2014; USGS SIM 3292)
access_method: Direct GIS (shapefile) download -> rasterise to 2 deg majority unit
notes: Lookup by unit: *v units (e.g. AHv, lHv) -> volcanic; Noachian highland (*Nh*) and impact units -> impact_mixed; lowland/transition/basin units (*l*, *t*, *b*) -> sedimentary; polar units (*p*) -> icy; clay_sulfate: no global unit - tag only cells with known clay/sulfate detections (e.g. Mawrth Vallis, Meridiani) or drop the word on Mars.

dataset: MGS MOLA DEM 463 m (MEGDR mosaic)
notes: NASA CORE PRIMARY. Compute slope at 463 m then 2-deg cell median.

dataset: MGS MOLA DEM 463 m
units: m (std. dev. of detrended elevation in the same ~3x3 km window as Earth; cell median)
notes: NASA CORE. Same window as Earth.

dataset: Constant (no liquid precipitation; hyper-arid everywhere)
notes: Recommend treating dryness as an Earth-only 'Mars-likeness' term (drier Earth cell = better) rather than a feature matched by rank, since it doesn't vary on Mars.

dataset: Global Permafrost Zonation Index (Gruber 2012)
licence: No restrictions; cite (UCAR Climate Data Guide)
notes: Primary perm_prob; Antarctica ice-free land set to 1 (assumed)

dataset: ESA CCI Permafrost extent v4.0 (PFR; NH)
licence: ESA CCI data policy; cite DOI
notes: Use instead of Gruber PZI north of 30N if downloaded

dataset: Global 1-km Gridded Thickness of Soil, Regolith, and Sedimentary Deposit Layers (Pelletier et al. 2016), average_soil_and_sedimentary-deposit_thickness.tif
notes: Bedrock rule in ground_label

dataset: MODIS Land Surface Temperature MOD11A2 v061 (day/night)
notes: Used in the Earth Engine export

dataset: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (2024_1 release)
notes: Release actually used in the export; also feeds roughness and elevation

dataset: SoilGrids 250 m v2.0 sand / clay / bulk density (0-200 cm)
notes: Used in the export (texture + density)
